module_catalog.name: International protection of persons with disabilities 806
module_catalog.content: The module focuses on principles and processes of international human rights law at the global level relevant to persons with disabilities. The selected topics include, but are not limited to the: (a) Introduction to relevant international human rights law principles, concepts and current issues relevant to persons with disabilities. (b) Introduction to disability as a social construct and basic concepts of  disability rights. (c) Historical trajectory of the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities at the global level. (d) Sources of International Law and their relevance to disability rights. (e) Development of soft law and treaty law for the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities prior to the CRPD, and the historical developments leading to the adoption of the CRPD. (f) Purpose, scope and definitions of the CRPD. (g) Substantive and procedural protection of the rights of persons with  disabilities under the CRPD and its Optional Protocol, including but not limited to the specific rights, general principles and obligations, and international cooperation of State parties. (h) Understand and analyse the monitoring mechanisms (international and national) and the requirements under the CRPD and its Optional Protocol. (i) Understand and analyse the Committee on the Rights of Persons  with Disabilities, as the monitoring body of the CRPD. (j) Understand and critically analyse selected United Nation  jurisprudence on disability rights. (k) Incorporation of the Convention into domestic law, constitutional  requirements and implementation measures. (l) Selected contemporary issues surrounding the CRPD and its Optional Protocol.

module_catalog.name: Applied international law 801
module_catalog.content: The module deals with the principles of international law at an advanced level. It focuses on theoretical questions pertaining to sources of the law and the relationship between international and national law. It analyses new developments in international law such as the changing content of sovereignity and the phenomenon of regional integration.

module_catalog.name: Mini-dissertation 800
module_catalog.content: The student must submit a research proposal during his/her first year of registration for the LLM degree to the supervisor prior to commencing with the writing of the mini-dissertation. A mini-dissertation (MND 800) of 13 000 to 15 000 words inclusive of footnotes but excluding the list of contents and the bibliography, is required. The mini-dissertation must be submitted to the supervisor not later than August of the second year of registration for the LLM programme. The mini-dissertation must deal with the subject content of one of the modules or a combination of the modules registered for by the student for his/her LLM degree. Any request for an extension of the period for submission of the mini-dissertation may only be granted by the Dean on recommendation of the LLM Committee
